title: TokenFlow health-check suite refactor and expand core model coverage
creator: Asha Mehta
description:
Summary:
We will refactor the existing tokens-per-second microbench harness into a new TokenFlow health-check suite that is easier to extend across core models and workload modes (cold/k versus warm/KV cache, batched vs single-request, small vs long contexts). The goal is to provide deterministic daily health checks, CI gating, and a lightweight regression detector that surfaces p95 regressions and token/sec degradations per-model and per-config.

Why this work:
- Current microbench code is fragmented and model onboarding requires manual steps.
- We need stable, reproducible measurements (tokens/sec and p95) that are comparable across hardware and quantization variants.
- Early detection of regressions reduces customer impact and debugging time.

Scope in this ticket:
- Introduce TokenFlow harness (python-based runner + lightweight agent) with config-driven workloads.
- Standardize measurement windows and percentile calculation (sliding window, warmup exclusion, header for KV cache warm/cold).
- Add per-model profiling templates and golden baselines for 3 canonical models (small, medium, large).
- Integrate a regression detector that compares nightly runs vs baseline and opens alerts if thresholds exceeded.
- Add a CI job that runs a smoke configuration on every runtime merge to catch obvious TPS regressions.

Out of scope for this ticket:
- Large-scale sustained-load harness (handled by ENG-32745).
- Automated model retraining or automatic fallback; only detection and alerting to start.
acceptance_criteria:
1) TokenFlow can run reproducible microbench workloads (cold/KV-warm, batched, single-stream) against all core models via a single config file.
2) Results include tokens/sec and p95 with warmup removed, and are written to JSON and CSV artifacts.
3) Nightly job compares last run to model-specific baseline and posts a regression report if tokens/sec drops >8% or p95 increases >15%.
4) CI smoke job runs on pull requests and fails with a clear artifact link on >20% TPS regression for the smoke config.
5) Documentation added for onboarding a new model and updating baselines.
implementation_notes:
- Runner will be a thin Python CLI (tokenflow-run) using existing runtime SDK for request orchestration.
- Use a YAML workload descriptor: model, prompt pattern, sequence length distribution, batch sizes, kv_cache_state.
- Measurement: exclude first 10% of requests as warmup, compute p50/p95/p99 and tokens/sec over the stable window.
- Store baselines in S3 under s3://redwood-bench/tokenflow/baselines/{model}/{hardware}/{quant}.
- Regression detector: simple percent-change comparator with configurable alert thresholds and cooldown.
- Keep the harness lightweight so it can run on a single c5 instance for CI smoke and on dedicated perf runners for nightly runs.
- Follow existing infra conventions for metrics and dashboarding (OpenTelemetry + Prometheus pushgateway integration).
test_plan:
- Unit tests for workload parser and percentile calculations.
- Local run against a dev model image to validate cold vs warm KV scenarios.
- CI smoke job added to runtime PR pipeline (runs small config).
- Nightly job: run against target models, upload artifacts, run detector, create a GitHub issue or PagerDuty alert for regressions.
- Cross-validate token/sec numbers vs older microbench reference for parity on the same hardware.
rollout_plan:
1) Merge TokenFlow harness behind feature flag.
2) Add CI smoke job and monitor for 1 week, adjust thresholds to reduce noise.
3) Enable nightly runs for the core model set.
4) After 2 successful nights of stable results, flip feature flag and replace legacy microbench invocations.
5) Announce to infra/perf channels and add docs to runbook.
